note: Every numeric constant of the process engine, with its unit and source. Python and TypeScript engines both read this file; scripts/check_units.py rejects undeclared literals in engine modules and entries without unit or source.

grid.top_um.source: Design: upper bound of the coarsest class, above the catalog crusher feed's 60 mm F80; the 2.5% of that Rosin-Rammler feed above it is lumped into the top class (review of 2026-10-04, C-09).

grid.n_classes.source: Design: the pan boundary falls at 3.24 um.

bond.lab_constant.unit: kWh per short ton, with the screen in um and the grindability in g/rev
bond.lab_constant.source: Bond (1961), in the form stated by Nikolic, Doll and Trumic (2022), doi:10.1016/j.mineng.2022.107822 (from the search summary, UNVERIFIED against the full text): Wi = 44.5 / (P1^0.23 Gbp^0.82 (10/sqrt(P80) - 10/sqrt(F80))) (RS-02).

bond.lab_screen_exponent.source: Bond (1961), as bond.lab_constant: the exponent of the closing screen P1.

bond.lab_grindability_exponent.source: Bond (1961), as bond.lab_constant: the exponent of the grindability Gbp.

bond.reference_feed_um.source: Design: reference reduction at which Rittinger and Kick are calibrated to Bond.

bond.reference_product_um.source: Design: reference reduction at which Rittinger and Kick are calibrated to Bond.

mill.mixer_fractions.source: Austin, Klimpel and Luckie (1984): one large and two equal small perfect mixers; the fractions are this product's declared values.

water.density_t_m3.source: Process water at plant temperature, rounded.

oracles.input_match_relative.source: Design: a published input the oracle re-solves (P80, circulating load) counts as met within this relative error; the solver closes to about 1e-13.

learning.coverage_floor.source: Design: a held-out fold whose 95% intervals cover fewer than 80% of its rows is counted as under-covered in the learning findings.

plitt.d50_coefficient.source: Plitt (1976) CIM Bull. 69(776):114-123, as documented in SysCAD Hydrocyclone.

flotation.sb_factor.source: Sb = 6 Jg/D32 (Gorain et al. 1997) with Jg in cm/s and D32 in mm.

savassi.constant.source: Savassi et al. (1998) Miner. Eng. 11(3):243-256, as typeset in Hoang et al. (2019) eq. 3.

batch.times_min.source: Design: laboratory batch-flotation sampling schedule for the virtual test.

numerics.recycle_rel_tolerance.source: Numerics: largest per-class relative change between recycle passes at convergence, so trace minerals close as tightly as the bulk (PE-02).

numerics.composite_scale_tolerance.source: Numerics: largest per-class change of the host-limited composite scale at convergence in the grinding circuit.

numerics.composite_scale_max_iterations.source: Numerics: iteration cap of the host-limited composite fixed point.

numerics.laguerre_nodes.source: Numerics: Gauss-Laguerre order for the residence-time projection.

grinding.energy_bracket_kwh_t.unit: kWh per t of mill feed per pass

grinding.cut_mode_load_max.source: Authored (E-01, review of 2026-10-02): the cut mode refuses a state whose circulating load exceeds 600%. Plant practice reports loads up to about 600% in secondary statements; the primary sources (Neesse et al. 2004, Minerals Engineering 17:1237-1240) were not opened. Data contract 02 states the refusal.

grinding.cut_mode_load_range.source: Design (CM-03): the circulating loads the target mode accepts as an input (Contract 1, 100 to 400%); a cut-mode state whose achieved load leaves it is flagged.

flotation.composite_surface_exponent.source: Declared: the exposed valuable surface of a composite grain scales with the two-thirds power of the valuable's volume fraction in the particle, phi = (c/rho_V)/(c/rho_V + (1 - c)/rho_host) for a mass content c; until 0.09.000 the mass content itself was raised to 2/3, which overstated composite rates by 7 to 47% (review of 2026-10-04, F-01).

numerics.negative_mass_tolerance.unit: 1 (class mass over that mineral's flow in the stream)
numerics.negative_mass_tolerance.source: Numerics: a class mass below minus this share of its own mineral's flow in the stream raises a negative-mass flag. Until 0.09.000 the tolerance was 1e-9 t/h per t/h of throughput, which could not see a trace mineral: a -2.3e-7 t/h electrum class, 7% of its stream's electrum, passed (review of 2026-10-04, K-10).

numerics.balance_tolerance.source: Numerics: a unit whose closure (per mineral, per size class where no breakage acts, per species, water, and the steady-state residual of a breakage operator) errs by more than this raises balance_not_closed (review of 2026-10-04, K-01); the same bound the envelope gate holds.

bond.efficiency_min_product_um.source: GMG01-MP-2021, sections 2 and 4.1 (Bond 1962): the Bond efficiency should not be applied to circuits with a P80 finer than about 70 um without qualification, the ball-mill fineness correction applying below it; the engine flags the state and does not apply the correction (review of 2026-10-04, C-02).

numerics.curve_class_share_floor.source: Numerics: a size class holding less than this share of the rougher-feed payable is reported empty (null) in the recovery-by-size curve; below it the class composition is round-off of the cyclone split, and the float64 ratio error grows as 1e-16 over the share.

numerics.cut_mode_load_tolerance.unit: 1 (relative to the circulating load, at least 1)
numerics.cut_mode_load_tolerance.source: Numerics (CM-02): the cut mode's fixed point on the circulating load stops when two passes agree within this; measured to converge at all 1,020 states of the cut-mode measurement (docs/design/features/cut-mode).

numerics.cut_mode_load_max_iterations.source: Numerics (CM-02): cap on the passes of the cut mode's fixed point; the measurement needed at most 20.

numerics.cut_search_step_ratio.source: Numerics: geometric step of the cut-size bracket search.

deslime.max_cut_over_p80.source: Design: the operating contract's rule deslime_cut_above_half_target (a coarser cut discards the product, page 08); the contract checks it against the grind target, and in the cut mode, where the target is ignored, the engine checks it against the achieved P80 and refuses the state (review of 2026-10-04, K-02).

numerics.cell_tail_tolerance.unit: 1 (relative change of a cell's tail flow)
numerics.cell_tail_tolerance.source: Numerics: convergence of a flotation cell's tail flow, the fixed point q = Q_tail(tau = V (1 - eps_g)/q) of the single-cell balance (F-02); solved by secant from the feed flow, measured to settle in under ten steps.

numerics.fit_bound_tolerance.unit: 1 (relative distance of a fitted parameter to its bound)
numerics.fit_bound_tolerance.source: Numerics: a kinetic fit whose bounded parameter (R_inf, phi, beta) lies within this relative distance of its bound is reported at that bound (F-07); the logistic reparameterization saturates there in double precision.

kinetics.signal_floor.source: Design: a virtual batch curve that ends below this recovery has no signal to fit; the record says so instead of reporting five unidentified fits (F-08).

numerics.load_log_floor.source: Numerics: added to the circulating load before its logarithm in the cut search, so a zero load reads as a finite value on the low-load side instead of an infinity the root finder would read as the high side (K-11); it changes no positive load in double precision.

numerics.power_limit_tolerance.unit: 1 (relative change of the energy per pass)
numerics.power_limit_tolerance.source: Numerics: convergence of the power limit's fixed point, e = P_inst over the mill feed of the pass at e; the mill feed moves with e only through the gravity unit's take (C-03).

numerics.energy_guess_floor_kwh_t.source: Numerics: floor of the Bond-based starting guess for the energy search.

kinetics.beta_bounds.source: Declared: range of the exponent that keeps the model identifiable on a nine-point batch curve; above 1 the curve has a delayed onset (compressed), below 1 it reflects a spread of rates (stretched); methodology page 11; Vinnett and Waters (2025), doi:10.1016/j.mineng.2025.109246.

kinetics.dense_points.source: Design: samples of each fitted curve from 0 to the last batch time (0.25 min spacing over 16 min), for plotting from the record.

numerics.lm_damping_factor.source: Numerics: damping decrease on an accepted step and increase on a rejected one.

numerics.lm_damping_bounds.source: Numerics: damping limits; reaching the upper one means no step lowers the residual in double precision.

numerics.lm_diagonal_floor.source: Numerics: floor on the diagonal of the normal matrix used for Marquardt scaling.

minerals.bornite_floatability_ratio.source: Authored, an upper bound (RS-03b): Jiang et al. (2025, Minerals 15:1148, doi:10.3390/min15111148, abstract only) report chalcopyrite above 90% in every collector system and bornite at 84.2% at best; with first-order kinetics at equal time, ln(1 - 0.842) / ln(1 - 0.90) = 0.80 (methodology page 15).

minerals.chalcocite_to_bornite_floatabil.source: Authored (RS-03b): Tafirenyika et al. (2022, Minerals 12:1527, doi:10.3390/min12121527), Table 3, plant water: at pH 9 ln(0.60)/ln(0.65) = 1.19 and at pH 11 ln(0.45)/ln(0.66) = 1.92, geometric mean 1.5; mass recoveries of impure samples (dossier of 2026-09-30).

optimization.starts.unit: unit cube of the decision bounds
optimization.starts.source: Design: five fixed starts that, with the variant's own point, make the six pattern-search starts; the magnetite circuit uses the first coordinate of each.

optimization.mesh_initial.unit: unit cube of the decision bounds
optimization.mesh_initial.source: Numerics (OP-02): the pattern search's initial mesh size, a quarter of each decision range; a power of two, so the browser takes the same steps.

optimization.mesh_minimum.unit: unit cube of the decision bounds
optimization.mesh_minimum.source: Numerics (OP-02): the pattern search stops below this mesh size, 2^-10 of each decision range (0.2 um of a 225 um grind range).

optimization.max_evaluations.source: Numerics (OP-02): cap on circuit evaluations per pattern-search start.

optimization.weight_default.source: Design (OP-01): the baked record's weight on recovered metal; 1 is recovered metal alone, the objective since 0.05.000.

optimization.weight_path.source: Design (OP-07): the weights on recovered metal at which the record keeps the optimum, each warm-started from the previous one.

optimization.weight_pct_bounds.source: Design (OP-10): the workbench's weight on recovered metal, in whole percent so the one validator checks its step in integers; the optimizer divides it by 100, which is exact at the recorded weights.

optimization.feasibility_tolerance.source: Numerics: a point is feasible when every constraint holds within this relative tolerance.

optimization.active_tolerance.source: Design: a constraint whose relative slack at the optimum is below this is reported as active.

optimization.decrease_tolerance.unit: 1 (relative to max(1, |objective|); relative for the violation)
optimization.decrease_tolerance.source: Numerics (OP-08): a trial point, a screened candidate or a start counts as better only by more than this. The engines in Python and TypeScript agree to round-off, and where the objective is flat (the free-milling gold's recovery at its optimum, equal to 5e-16) a comparison of equal values could otherwise decide differently in the two languages; improvements this small are below anything the mesh resolves.

optimization.screen_steps.source: Design (OP-05): the screen's candidates lie these many mesh steps from each incumbent along every coordinate; one step is the poll's own points, two the points beyond them.

optimization.screen_half_width_pct.source: Design (OP-05): the screen proposes a candidate only where the Gaussian process's 95% half-width on recovery is at most this; about half the lane's mean held-out half-width (9.3 points in the 0.06.000 learning record), so the surrogate is trusted only where it is more confident than on an average interpolation state.

uncertainty.half_widths.unit: fraction of the variant value (uniform on 1 - h to 1 + h)
uncertainty.half_widths.source: Authored: ore-property spreads for the uncertainty and sensitivity records; not fitted to a deposit, stated as such on the Methodology page.

uncertainty.samples.source: Design: Monte Carlo sample size of the uncertainty record (PE-28).

uncertainty.seed.source: Design: seed of the SplitMix64 Latin hypercube, so every record is reproducible and the browser repeats it (UQ-01 to UQ-05).

uncertainty.seed_bounds.source: Design (UQ-07): a seed the workbench accepts, from 0 to 2^53 - 1, the largest integer a browser number holds exactly.

studies.seed_study_seeds.source: Design (Experiments, uncertainty): eight seeds, distinct from the bake's, at which every nominal uncertainty record is re-run to measure the design's own sampling error.

uncertainty.samples_bounds.source: Design (UQ-07): the workbench's sample count, minimum, maximum and step; 512 engine runs take about half a minute in the browser.

uncertainty.quantiles.source: Design: P05, P50 and P95 of each output (PE-28).

sensitivity.base_samples.source: Design: Saltelli base sample N (a power of two); first- and total-order indices need N (D + 2) circuit evaluations.

sensitivity.resamples.source: Design: bootstrap resamples for the 95% confidence intervals of the Sobol indices (SALib).

sensitivity.confidence.source: Design: confidence level of the Sobol index intervals.

sensitivity.constant_tolerance.source: Numerics: an output whose spread across the design is below this share of its magnitude is constant up to round-off (the grinding energy of a mill at installed power at every sample); Sobol indices of it would apportion floating-point noise, so it is recorded as constant.

learning.design_points_per_case.source: Design: engine states per case in the learning design (a power of two for the Sobol sequence).

learning.seed.source: Design: seed of the learning design, the splits and every model.

learning.test_fraction.source: Design: share of each case's states held out by the interpolation protocol.

learning.validation_fraction.source: Design: share of the training rows held out for early stopping and for the guard threshold.

learning.ridge_alpha.source: Design: L2 penalty of the linear reference model on standardized features.

learning.forest_trees.source: Design: trees of the random forest (Breiman 2001).

learning.forest_min_leaf.source: Design: minimum samples per random-forest leaf.

learning.hgb_iterations.source: Design: boosting iterations of HistGradientBoostingRegressor (fixed, no internal early stopping).

learning.hgb_learning_rate.source: Design: shrinkage of the gradient-boosting surrogate.

learning.gp_training_rows.source: Design: seeded subsample the Gaussian process is fitted on (the exact GP costs O(n^3)).

learning.gp_restarts.source: Design: restarts of the GP marginal-likelihood optimizer.

learning.interval_z.source: Two-sided 95% quantile of the standard normal distribution, for GP interval coverage.

learning.mlp_hidden.source: Design: hidden layers of the multi-output MLP surrogate.

learning.mlp_learning_rate.source: Design: Adam step size (Kingma and Ba 2015).

learning.mlp_weight_decay.source: Design: decoupled weight decay of the MLP and the autoencoder.

learning.max_epochs.source: Design: epoch cap of the MLP and the autoencoder; training stops earlier on validation loss.

learning.patience.source: Design: epochs without a lower validation loss before training stops (the best weights are restored).

learning.autoencoder_hidden.source: Design: encoder, bottleneck and decoder widths of the out-of-envelope guard.

learning.guard_quantile.source: Design: the guard threshold is this quantile of the validation reconstruction error, so about 1% of in-envelope states raise a false alarm.

learning.ood_shift.source: Design: out-of-envelope probes move one feature this far beyond its training maximum.

learning.permutation_repeats.source: Design: repeats of permutation importance (Breiman 2001; scikit-learn permutation_importance).

learning.onnx_tolerance.source: Numerics: largest difference allowed between PyTorch and ONNX Runtime outputs of an exported model.

learning.gp_export_tolerance.source: Numerics (OP-05): largest difference allowed between the screen's float64 Gaussian process and scikit-learn's predict(return_std=True), in mean and standard deviation, at the export check.

units.short_ton_per_tonne.source: Exact: 1 short ton = 907.18474 kg; Bond's laboratory form gives kWh per short ton.

learning.gp_noise_initial.source: Design: starting noise level of the GP white-noise kernel; the marginal likelihood fits it.

learning.gp_noise_bounds.source: Design: white-noise bounds of the GP; the engine is deterministic, so the fitted noise is expected near the lower bound.

learning.gp_length_scale_bounds.source: Design: ARD length-scale bounds; a length scale at the upper bound means the feature is switched off.

learning.gp_bound_margin.source: Design: a fitted length scale above this share of its upper bound is reported as switched off.

cyclone.grg_density_exponent.source: Fitted to the GRG and solids partition curves of Laplante and Staunton (AMIRA P420B), Figure 9: 1.13 at Jundee, 0.87 at Marvel Loch. Stokes' 0.5 puts the GRG cut two to four times too coarse there (2.2 at Marvel Loch, 3.8 at Jundee; the fit used the ore at SG 2.75 as the reference, and on quartz at 2.65 it gives 0.85 and 1.10); every other mineral keeps 0.5 for want of a measurement of its own (review of 2026-10-02, E-11; review of 2026-10-04, P-01).

gravity.grg_selection_sizes_um.source: The centres of Banisi's two size ranges, 50 to 100 um and 500 to 1000 um (cited by Vincent 1997, McGill M.Eng. thesis, chapter 5).

gravity.grg_selection_slowdown.source: Banisi measured gold breaking six times slower than the ore at 50 to 100 um and twenty times slower at 500 to 1000 um, from its malleability (cited by Vincent 1997, chapter 5). Interpolated in log-log between the range centres and held constant outside.

learning.ood_shifts.unit: fraction of the feature's training range
learning.ood_shifts.source: Authored (M-16, review of 2026-10-02): the guard's acceptance of out-of-envelope probes is reported over these distances, above the maximum and below the minimum, instead of at 0.5 of a range above only.

learning.mlp_seed_offsets.source: Authored (M-21, review of 2026-10-02): the network's transfer numbers are reported over five training seeds; the offset 0 is the record's own seed.
